articleTitle: P-Swish: Activation Function with Learnable Parameters Based on Swish Activation Function in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In order to improve the performance of a deep neural network, the activation function is an important aspect that we must research continuously, that is why we have expanded the research in this direction. We introduced a novel P-Swish activation function (Parametric Swish), which is able to bring performance improvements on object classification tasks using datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, but we will see that we also used datasets for Natural Language Processing (NLP). To test it, we used several types of architectures, including LeNet-5, Network in Network (NiN), and ResNet34 compared to popular activation functions such as sigmoid, ReLU, Swish, and our proposals. In particular, the P-Swish function facilitates fast network training, which makes it suitable for the Transfer Learning technique.

articleTitle: End-to-End Computer Vision Framework
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Computer Vision is a cross research field with the main purpose of understanding the surrounding environment as closely as possible to human perception. In addition to research on techniques and algorithms that enhance the capabilities of a Computer Vision system, research on the architecture and design of such systems is also important. In this paper we present an End-to-End Computer Vision Framework open-source solution, based on Python programming language, that aims to support researchers in this field. The main focus of the framework is the configurability and scalability of the system in the continuous need to add new Computer Vision algorithms or machine learning models for a day-to-day research activity.

articleTitle: Image encryption algorithm using wavelet packets and multiple chaotic maps
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved image encryption algorithm using Haar wavelet packets decomposition and four chaotic maps. For the wavelet packets scrambling we propose a permutation based on the Baker chaotic map. To increase the entropy of the ciphered image and the key space of the cryptosystem two chaotic maps - the three-dimensional Arnold map, applied twice, and the tent map combined with the logistic map - are used. Matlab simulations show that, in each step, these chaotic maps increase the entropy of the encrypted images and the pixels' decorrelation. Another benefit obtained using the four maps is the augmentation of the key space.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Eye Gaze Tracking for Automotive Applications: An Auto-Keras Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose a deep neural network-based gaze sensing method in which the design of the neural architecture is performed automatically, through a network architecture search algorithm called Auto-Keras. First, the neural model is generated using the Columbia Gaze Data Set. Then, the performance of the solution is estimated on an online scenario and proves the generalization ability of our model. In comparison to a geometrical approach, which uses dlib facial landmarks, filtering and morphological operators for gaze estimation, the proposed method provides superior results and certain advantages.

articleTitle: Structuring, Controlling and Protecting the DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The structure of a DC grid enables control and protection in a different way, as usually employed in AC grids. Power electronic converters combine the control and protection. The structure of the DC grid is also determined by the type of power electronic converters being centralized or decentralized. Power congestion management greatly improves the DC grid. Although power electronics means extra losses per converter, so a lower efficiency, the DC grid can be used more efficient than the AC grid.

articleTitle: Education 4.0: Smart Blended Learning Assisted by Artificial Intelligence, Biofeedback and Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents smart blended learning for fostering students’ performance. It uses models of student activity and detects causes of a possible drop out, using learning analytics and real-time data. Taking advantage of embedded sensors (non-invasive, low-cost, flexible and distraction free) built into wearable devices real-time data can be used to support students’ success, well-being and health. In our contribution to the research topic we evaluate the students' experience with smart blended learning using biofeedback methods, sensor data extracted from wearables for five specific lectures, during study periods and in examinations. The preliminary results indicate a correlation between the physiological signals and the grades in examination.

articleTitle: Security threats in IoT
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a massive group of devices connected over wired or wireless networks. IoT aims to provide advanced and intelligent services but at the same time to ensure security. It is a challenge to find lightweight security models and techniques as the IoT devices have low resources and low computing power. As a result, IoT devices became a target of cyber-attacks because of deficiency in safety mechanism. This paper discusses the vulnerabilities of IoT devices and several security challenges. It contains some detailed implementation and analysis of IoT oriented attacks and some security solutions.

articleTitle: LMS Algorithms for Multilinear Forms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Solving a high-dimension system identification problem could involve significant challenges in terms of complexity and accuracy of the solution. Due to the large parameter space, a decomposition-based approach fits very well in this context. This was the idea behind the recently developed iterative Wiener filter for multilinear forms, which reformulates the problem using a combination of shorter filters. Nevertheless, there are inherent limitations related to the Wiener solution, while the least-mean-square (LMS) adaptive filter would represent a more practical alternative. Consequently, in this paper, we develop LMS-based algorithms for multilinear forms, in the context of a multiple-input/single-output system identification problem. Simulation results indicate the good performance of the proposed algorithms, especially in terms of their fast convergence features.

articleTitle: EMC Simulation of an Automotive Ethernet Interface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A case study concerning application of full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulation for identifying issues that usually appear at an Ethernet interface from an Automotive module is reported in this paper. By using 3D full EM simulation, the time-to-market of an automotive product can be reduced, by skipping expensive and time-consuming investigations in laboratory. The work has started from the necessity of Automotive products to have Ethernet requirements met, especially the ones related to Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC). Namely, mode conversion loss and return loss are investigated and several possible solutions for improvement have been considered.

articleTitle: IoT Based Intelligent Building Applications in the Context of COVID-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: COVID-19 (Coronavirus) has affected our day to day life and the global economy and is far from being over. COVID-19 continues to spread rapidly around the world, more with the relaxation of restriction measures imposed by most countries. Limiting the further community spread of the epidemic has become a crucial issue, as employees return to office buildings. Technology, and especially intelligent building technology, can help to this purpose. Smart devices will have an important role to play in determining how the new normal workplace will function from now on. In this paper, we propose a solution for avoiding touching various objects and surfaces in offices, based on IoT. The system is called qToggle and provides a framework for efficiently and effectively interconnecting smart devices, equipping them with intelligence that helps automating many of the everyday activities in offices. Most qToggle devices are based on ESP8266/ESP8285 chips, Raspberry Pi boards and smart sensors. A mobile application allows users to control a series of appliances and sensors.

articleTitle: Integrating Service Robots into Everyday Life Based on Audio Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a way in which TIAGo, a service robot from Pal Robotics, could be integrated in everyday life, based on his audio capabilities. We show that using 20 Mel frequency cepstral coefficients and 5-nearest neighbors we rich an overall correct classification rate of 99.27% in the testing phase. However, we do not recommend non-MFCC features for implementations with the TIAGo service robot, at least for the framework presented in the current paper.

articleTitle: Analyzing parking lots vacancy detection algorithms using Mask R-CNN implementations
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Parking is a very common problem that the modern society is facing nowadays. Numerous countries are working to manage their current transportation systems and road infrastructure to enhance traffic flows, mobility, and safety. The city of Timisoara has already taken the first steps towards this in the past, but the city is still afflicted by excessive traffic. The aim of this paper is to present, analyze and compare two algorithms for detecting occupied and vacant spaces in the parking place using the Mask R-CNN implementations. The potential implications include a drastic reduction in parking time and, consequently, overall traffic.

articleTitle: Dynamic Spectrum Sharing for LTE-NR Downlink MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: 5G is the next mobile generation, already being deployed in some countries. It is expected to revolutionize our society, having extremely high target requirements. Moreover, it will bring new applications, new technologies, and increases on data rates, capacity, energy and spectrum efficiency, number of connected devices, among many others. The use of spectrum is, therefore, extremely important, since it is a limited and expensive resource, from the operator point of view. A solution for the spectrum efficiency is the use of DSS, where an operator can share the spectrum between two different technologies. This paper investigates the impact of the DSS feature for an LTE-NR system. Performance results are analyzed in terms of throughput and show that DSS constitutes a good feature for the future mobile systems, with an increase of spectrum efficiency and cost reduction.

articleTitle: A New Step-Up Converter With Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper proposes a new step-up converter with coupled inductor, one active switch and three diodes that work as a Boost converter. Compared to the classical Boost converter, the novel topology provides a higher static conversion ratio at the same duty cycle. The proposed converter finds suitability in conversion where an output voltage much higher than the input voltage is required. A dc analysis is performed to obtain the static characteristic of the converter. Also, the design equations are provided, and the converter is simulated and experimentally tested in order to confirm the feasibility of the proposed step-up converter with coupled inductor.

Author Keywords: static conversion ratio and step-up converter

articleTitle: Modelling an OPC UA client application for predictive maintenance support
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is a very important task for each industrial plant. The concept of Industry 4.0 can ensure this service, offering a clever combination of many technologies. This paper presents a method for deploying a software application that provides the maintenance personnel with a useful tool, allowing them to follow the parameters of the process and to prevent its failure. The application has a client-server structure and uses the open platform communications unified architecture (OPC UA) standard and unified architecture transport control protocol (UA TCP) for data communication. The application developed using the proposed method is meant to be a predictive maintenance tool for the blower station of a wastewater treatment plant, so that the maintenance personnel have the necessary data as system health indicators. The maintenance client software shows the personnel the current functional state of the process by synoptic screens. When the maintenance procedures require it, different process states or process parameter values can be accessed from a dedicated Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) database and provide important information to the maintenance personnel (MP).

articleTitle: Containerized Application for IoT Devices: Comparison between balenaCloud and Amazon Web Services Approaches
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Depending on the requirements, the deployment of containerized applications for monitoring Internet of Things devices can be done in Cloud or on the Edge. This paper discusses the design of a containerized application monitoring temperature and humidity for IoT devices in three implementations: (1) balenaCloud for edge deployment; (2) Amazon Web Services cloud with EC2 instances; and (3) dedicated Amazon Web Services IoT service. The experiments showed that there are no significant performance differences between Edge and Cloud deployments regarding the resource consumption. However, for fast and almost effortless action, Amazon Web Services IoT is the go-to option when it comes to serverless applications based on Message Queuing Telemetry Transport. For all-in-one automated fleet management balenaCloud seems to be a good tool for IoT developers.

articleTitle: Deep CNN for Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Focal Liver Lesions Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper investigates the huge potential provided by the deep learning paradigm associated with a convolutional neural network architecture for automatic diagnosis of focal liver lesions. The dataset was provided by the Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, "Victor Babes" University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Timisoara and contains a total of 285 contrast-enhanced ultrasound video sequences of five types of lesions. As elements of novelty of our work we could mention the use of 2D-Deep Convolutional Neural Network for implementing an automated diagnosis system which discriminates between an increased number of focal liver lesion types. Our experimental results demonstrated that the proposed principle achieves a competitive performance, 95.71% accuracy, compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Aspects of Time Series Analysis with Entropies and Complexity Measures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This exploratory work looks on time series complexity, for direct applications in change detection of the structure and properties of the signals. The objective of the paper was to compare the results of the evaluation of the complexity of time series data, obtained with measures based on entropy and data complexity indices. As test signals, determinist, random and chaotic signals are considered, in an independent and mixed probabilistic approach. Complexity descriptors are based on entropies, as Renyi, Tsallis, Multiscale technique, and two data complexity indices, as Lempel-Ziv complexity and Lyapunov exponent. High values of complexity measures are expected for all cases where random or chaotic components are dominant, i.e. greater amplitudes than the determinist components. The complexity measures are evaluated in terms of monotony, sensitivity at the length of time series, and change detection capability of the structure of the analyzed signal. The results of the experiments based on computer-based simulations are presented with fuzzy labels and show a variety of results, i.e. good results for some cases and small for others. Such results suggest an aggregate criterion for change detection, with at least two terms, one based on entropy and another one on complexity indices.

articleTitle: Traffic Engineering and QoS in a Proposed MPLS-VPN
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper comes with a solution to the use of multiple simultaneous applications (data and voice) in a secure trouble-free environment. More exactly, it presents a network based not only on hybrid MPLS-VPN (Multiprotocol Label Switching - Virtul Private Network), but also on Quality of Service and Traffic Engineering. The main purpose of this work is to assure no congestion or delays on the routes of the customers and to make space for the allocation of resources for different communication sessions.

articleTitle: Head Gesture Recognition based on 6DOF Inertial sensor using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposed and investigated the head gesture recognition idea based on a single inertial sensor and deep learning approach. During the experiments presented in this paper, the main aim was to evaluate and determine the best deep learning models that can accurately recognize the head movements. The developed system can identify eight head gestures activities. The data collected in this work was done using a 6DOF inertial sensor placed on a headphone pair from 9 volunteers with ages between 20 and 40 years old. The results show that the best-proposed model's classification accuracy did reach a value equal to 93.64 % using raw data. In this experiment, each head gesture command's accuracy was in the range of 71.11 % to 100 %.

articleTitle: Monopulse Secondary Surveillance Radar Antenna Theory
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article brings clarifications regarding the implementation of a Monopulse Secondary Surveillance Radar (MSSR) antenna. The calculations focus on SUM beam patterns in the radar-aircraft dialogue. The novelty is the determination, by calculation, of the vertical SUM beam pattern. For the chosen antenna design, the same working algorithm can be applied to determine the CONTROL and DIFFERENCE beam patterns.

articleTitle: Modified Langendorff experimental device for rat heart decellularization with a vibrating fluid column
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the present paper we propose the design and realization of an experimental device of Langendorff type, controlled in pressure and with the vibrating column of fluid, used for decellularization of the rat heart with a surfactant solution of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). The experimental device consists of two constructive parts: a hydraulic-electronic part that ensures constant pressure for retrograde heart perfusion and an electromagnetic assembly that induces the vibration of the liquid column in the immediate vicinity of the device cannula with a frequency of 15 Hz. The decellularization solution is recirculated during the experiment, so that by serial spectrophotometric determinations of the concentration of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and proteins in this solution can determine the kinetics of decellularization and the moment when it is completed.

articleTitle: TeLU: A New Activation Function for Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we proposed two novel activation functions, which we called them TeLU and TeLU learnable. These proposals are a combination of ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), tangent(tanh), and ELU (Exponential Linear Units) without and with a learnable parameter. We prove that the activation functions TeLU and TeLU learnable give better results than other popular activation functions, including ReLU, Mish, TanhExp, using current architectures tested on Computer Vision datasets.

articleTitle: IoT Applications based on MQTT Protocol
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents two different approaches for implementing IoT applications, using the MQTT protocol. The paradigm is discussed from a security point of view. The components of the first system are two Raspberry PI boards (model 4 and model 3B+), a breadboard with LEDs and an IFTTT application. The tools used for the analysis of potential threats are from the Kali Linux distribution. The second approach was the usage of the ThingsBoard platform that enables the integration of different IoT devices into one system.

articleTitle: Extending the libtins library with SIP and RTP classes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The libtins open-source library provides an accessible, cross-platform solution for sniffing and crafting network packets using the C++ programming language. Using the built-in functionality of the library, the user can capture, create, modify and send network packets. This paper aims to showcase the process of extending the libtins library with classes that define parsing methods for VoIP (Voice over IP) data, specifically focusing on the SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) and RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) protocols, with the goal of creating a packet analyzer application specialized for Voice over IP packet processing.

articleTitle: A New Multiphase ZVT-PWM Synchronous Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A new multiphase Zero-Voltage-Transition (ZVT) Pulse-Width Modulated (PWM) synchronous buck converter is presented in this paper. With an auxiliary circuit, all switches of buck converter can be operated under soft switching conditions. The evaluation is well verified on a 2 kW two phase ZVT- PWM synchronous buck converter and the experiment efficiency compared with ordinary two phase buck converter is given.

articleTitle: Novel Software Defined Radio Testbed for Spectrum Occupancy Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The radio frequency spectrum is a key resource that must be considered during the development of current wireless communication systems. As it is a limited resource, it is of crucial importance to use it in an efficient way. In this paper we propose a spectrum occupancy measurement testbed based on software defined radio (SDR) platforms. Spectrum occupancy measurement campaigns conducted in an urban and a suburban location using the proposed testbed are also presented. The measurement results are commented and show that the proposed SDR based testbed is a viable solution for the spectrum occupancy evaluation. It is highlighted that one of the possible solutions for improving the spectrum usage efficiency is the dynamic spectrum access (DSA) approach, that was already considered in case of 4G networks and is also an important aspect considered for design of the 5G physical layer.

articleTitle: Contrasts Comparison of Same Cases of Chest Pathologies for Radiography and Tomosynthesis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article considers the possibility of using digital X-ray tomosynthesis for the computer automatic diagnosis of lung pathologies, including the detection of the early stages of pneumonia (including caused by COVID-19) and tuberculosis. The advantages of this method in comparison with digital radiography and computed tomography are shown. Digital tomosynthesis is considered as an additional option, which is recommended to be installed on all existing basic radiographic systems with their transfer to digital technologies.

articleTitle: Preconditioned K-SVD for ECG Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose Preconditioned K-SVD, an algorithm for dictionary learning adapted for sparse coding with Least Squares Pursuit. The algorithm resembles K-SVD iterations but operates in a preconditioned signal space, which implies a different optimization goal then K-SVD, namely to minimize the norm of the cosupport coefficients in the sparse representations. The algorithm is designed to operate with sparse coding algorithms based on null space projections, e.g. Least Squares Pursuit. Simulation results in the context of ECG arrhythmia detection show a performance similar to K-SVD with Orthogonal Matching Pursuit sparse coding.

articleTitle: RD-CNN: A Compact and Efficient Convolutional Neural Net for Sound Classification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Classification of signals (sounds, biomedical, etc.) occurs in various circumstances, often requiring low-complexity implementations for various resources-constrained platforms such as mobile or embedded systems within the IoT framework. Herein we describe preliminary results for a novel recognition system where a compact and fast transform, the reaction-diffusion transform (RDT), is used to generate spectral images. Such images are then processed into a novel type of compact convolution neural network (called NL-CNN) where nonlinear convolution is emulated. The ESC-50 environmental sound database with 50 sound categories was considered for parameter tuning and performance evaluation. Despite its low complexity, a reasonable well accuracy is demonstrated (up to 76.5%) close to the human accuracy reported on the same dataset and better in both accuracy and complexity when compared to similar approaches reported in the literature and based on mel-cepstrum. These results provide a basis for a novel and effective method for time-series recognition in general.

articleTitle: Network Self-Similar Traffic Generator with Variable Hurst Parameter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Traffic modelling plays an essential role in the analysis of network performance. Network traffic exhibits self-similarity. We propose a self-similar traffic generator based on wavelets theory, which can be used for testing intrusion detection, congestion control and anomaly detection systems. The length of the traffic trace, the value of the Hurst's exponent and the expectation of the generated traffic process can be accurately set using the proposed algorithm. Simulations show that the proposed algorithm has the performance similar with state of the art traffic generation algorithms.

articleTitle: Cascaded adaptive filters in a bilinear approach for system identification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The multilinear concept allows extending the capacity of adaptive system identification to multiple input, long length or nonlinear systems. Because of the limited space, this paper refers only to the bilinear form. Some different physical structures that can be described by a bilinear input-output relation are presented. Two basic linear classes of elements, the weighted adder(combiner) and the FIR filters are used. From these structures, the weighted combiner-FIR filter is more present in literature. This paper focuses on the filter-filter structure, allowing identification by two cascaded filters. The adaptive algorithm is presented and some simulations are performed to validate the theory.

articleTitle: Spectrum Occupancy Measurements in the Wi-Fi Band with a PCB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Contemporary development of wireless communication networks caused an increase of electromagnetic interference signal levels in both indoor and outdoor environments. In this paper, a measurement equipment for the field intensity and spectrum occupancy based on a SDR platform and a PCB antenna is described. The equipment has been used for acquiring signals in the Wi-Fi frequency range. Spectrum occupancy has been measured based on an energy threshold detection criterion. Impact of polarization and direction of arrival on the spectrum of the received signal have been assessed.

articleTitle: Wavelet Based Adaptive Detection of Automotive Radar Single Target with Low SNR
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We propose an adaptive detection algorithm combining two signal processing methods: ordered statistics and wavelet based denoising, with the purpose of detecting low SNR single automotive radar target. The detection is realized by denoising the Range-Doppler map obtained for the Rapid Chirps waveform, using a Hard-Thresholding filter applied in the wavelet domain. The threshold is selected as the maximum value of the medians of the Range-Doppler map resolution cells. We quantify by simulations the merits of each of the two signal processing methods used.

articleTitle: On Using ReSpeaker Mic Array 2.0 for speech processing algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents the structure and applications achieved with a newly launched device called ReSpeaker Mic Array 2.0 (ReSpeaker 2 for short). This is a four microphones array that also contains the XMOS XVF-3000 chipset. This chipset includes many signal and speech processing algorithms. Thus the paper presents applications that mainly use the embedded software of XMOS but also applications that gather the four signals acquired by ReSpeaker 2 and implement the algorithms using another hardware platform. The applications present algorithms such as acoustic echo cancelation, direction of arrival for multiple sources, speech separation and speech to text conversion. ReSpeaker 2 is used with Raspberry Pi or a Personal Computer running Windows or Linux.

articleTitle: Multiple Radar Targets Tracking and Trajectories Fitting
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a data association and tracking algorithm followed by polynomial fitting, in the case of multiple radar targets to improve the accuracy of targets' trajectories estimated by an automotive radar sensor.Starting from the conjecture that any real trajectory is polynomial in cartesian coordinates the proposed method supposes to fit the data obtained at the output of Kalman filter to a polynomial. We used the polynomial fitting method for the trajectories of three targets, which we generated in two different scenarios. In both scenarios the targets could be tracked properly using Kalman filters after data association, and the trajectories were improved by applying the polynomial fitting.

articleTitle: Color quotient based mask detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper deals with mask detection in the age of COVID - 19, by proposing a simple and efficient method to detect people not wearing mask. The approach includes a feature extraction step followed by a supervised learning model built with support vector machines. The features are formed of color information by considering red, green and blue channels for an RGB color image. Ratio of color channels is taken into account to discriminate between mask and non mask images. The approach has been tested on a set of 1211 facial images extracted from group of people wearing or not wearing a mask, by considering a 2 - class problem, where the mask class represents the positive examples, where the non-masked faces are negative examples. Part of the image data set is used to train the support vector machines for learning discriminant features for each class, followed by a prediction for each test sample. The image set for the mask class ranges from simple and common one-colored surgical masks to complex and challenging patterned masks. Cross-validation approach is adopted to test the approach, leading to 97.25 % as recognition rate.

articleTitle: A Generalized Model for Single-Switch Stacked Step-Down Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper focuses on the generalization of two stage stacked step-down converter previously published. Thus, an n stage topology is obtained. The study insists on the dc conversion ratio and uses mathematical tools for studying the main properties. It is proved that for step-down ratios close to the unity a reasonable duty cycle can be used, compared to a classical buck, where high unobtainable duty cycles are required. The main dc inductor currents and capacitive voltages are calculated in order to facilitate converter design. Results are supported by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Volumetric Distributed Denial-of-Service and Session Replay Attacks-Resistant AAA-RADIUS Solution Based on EAP and LDAP
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The solution presented in this paper presents an improved security variant of standard implementations of the Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service protocol within a Service Provider's network. The Authentication, Authorization and Accounting mechanism may be subject to cyber-attacks with the effect of compromising the network. Therefore, it is necessary to implement an authentication protection solution against common cybersecurity attacks. For the presented solution, a unified protection module against Session Replay and Volumetric Distributed Denial-of-Service attacks has been developed and integrated within an AAA-RADIUS solution.

articleTitle: Improved 3D Co-Occurrence Matrix for Texture Description and Classification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved feature extraction method for volumetric texture classification. Our approach consists in the computation of 3D co-occurrence matrices built using both the image intensity and the gradient image information. The feature vector represents the concatenation of the Haralick second-order statistics and the proposed gradient-based and orientation-based indicators. The results obtained on a public synthetic 3D texture database show that the proposed technique is more discriminative and brings improvements in the classification performance when compared to recent 3D and 2D texture descriptors.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing based watermarking as a security layer for computational imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The evolution of digital imaging since its early days has mostly been driven by hardware advancements. Computational imaging is a recent alternative to traditional imaging, that focuses on the use of digital processing algorithms. One notable example is the single pixel imaging and its recent developments in the area of lensless imaging. It uses image acquisition based on the compressive sensing (CS) theory, resulting in measurement data that use less storage space. However, it requires more computational resources in order to reconstruct the image and make it available for the end user. The CS theory also opens new research opportunities regarding the security of digital image processing, storage and distribution. This paper presents a privacy enabling architecture for a real-life scenario of image acquisition using the single pixel camera. A reversible watermark is inserted to the measurement data before storage and distribution.

articleTitle: Intention prediction of car drivers at inner city junctions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this work an approach to reliably predict a driver's intention at a T-intersection is presented. Knowing the intention of oncoming drivers is especially helpful at unregulated intersections. We specifically focus on a scenario where the turning pattern generates a situation in which no driver has the right of way. Our approach utilizes only the trajectories of the vehicles that are involved. These can be observed directly and we therefore do not rely on any explicit communication between vehicles. From the trajectories several features are defined that serve as input for the classification algorithms. We use Random Forests and Conditional Random Fields in this work. To gain behavioral data of human drivers in unregulated situations, a study in a driving simulator was conducted.

articleTitle: First Fresnel Ellipse Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical formulas for the first Fresnel ellipse / ellipsoid, applied to the radio waves propagation. The final purpose is to check line-of-sight path condition and 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> Fresnel zone clearance, in order to use the free space formula for propagation loss calculation and required transmitted power, for a given geographic map and for different parameters of the transmitter - receiver link.

articleTitle: People Detection in a Depth Sensor Network via Multi-View CNNs trained on Synthetic Data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this work an approach for wide-area indoor people detection with a network of depth sensors is presented. We propose an end-to-end multi-view deep learning architecture which takes three foreground segmented overlapping depth images as input and predicts the marginal probability distribution of people present in the scene. In contrast to classical data-driven approaches our method does not make use of any real image data for training but uses a randomized generative scene model to generate synthetic depth images which are used to train our proposed deep learning architecture. The evaluation shows promising results on a publicly available data set.

articleTitle: Face Recognition Using Tensors and Gradient Descriptors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Face recognition algorithms are key issues in many applications, still challenging in terms of complexity and reliability. In this paper we propose a different approach for a solution based on tensors and multilinear singular value decomposition (MLSVD). We define a new tensorization of face image descriptors built into gradient space and rely on such feature vectors to identify a subject from the database. The tensor is decomposed using MLSVD model to form a linear set of equations with a Kronecker product solution. We show that our method lowers the computation complexity while keeping high accuracy in the recognition process.

articleTitle: Virtual Instrumentation based Prototype for Evaluation of the Cardiac Systolic Function
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a Virtual Instrumentation (VI) based prototype designed to evaluate systolic parameters resulting from the calculation of the Blumberger hemodynamic index (BHI) and the ejection fraction of the left ventricle (FEJ). In accordance with the available results, one can assess the cardiovascular activity of the patient. The proposed prototype includes integrated hardware and software, it is low-cost, noninvasive, and graphical user-friendly. Real-time cardiovascular signals representing the electrocardiographic derivation, the phonocardiogram and the peripheral photoplestismogram, are sampled using dedicated sensors, customized signal conditioning and an Arduino Uno device. Collected data is sent to a National Instruments' LabVIEW<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> application. An important feature of the proposed application allows the user to dynamically set measurement cursor limits by scrolling over the acquired waveforms plots. At the same time, calculation results are displayed, providing the means to perform an initial evaluation of the cardiovascular pathology. Functionality tests, performed with the help of several persons, confirm that the proposed system was properly designed and implemented. Consequently, it can become a suitable evaluation device in a family doctor or general medicine office, where the usage of professional equipment is not mandatory. This solution is also viable for educational purposes, especially in the case of medical instrumentation related subjects.

articleTitle: A New Quadratic Step-Down Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper proposes a new quadratic step-down converter with single active switch and three diodes that work as a buck converter, while it still operates at moderate duty cycles. The main static features of the converter are revealed after a dc analysis is performed. The main design equations are derived, then the converter is simulated and finally experimentally tested in order to validate and prove the feasibility of the proposed step-down quadratic topology.

Author Keywords: step-down quadratic converter and static voltage

articleTitle: A Regularized RLS Algorithm for the Identification of Third-Order Tensors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The recently proposed recursive least-squares (RLS) algorithm for trilinear forms, namely RLS-TF, was designed for the identification of third-order tensors of rank one. In this context, a high-dimension system identification problem can be efficiently addressed (gaining in terms of both performance and complexity) based on tensor decompositions and modelling. In this paper, following the framework of the RLS-TF, we propose a regularized version of this algorithm, where the regularization terms are incorporated within the cost functions. Furthermore, the optimal regularization parameters are derived, aiming at attenuating the effects of the system noise. Simulation results support the performance features of the proposed algorithm, especially in terms of its robustness in noisy environments.

articleTitle: An innovative algorithm for data differencing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We are presenting a novel algorithm to create software updates using Normalized Compression Distance (NCD) where we define the Z compression function as a modified LZ77[1] compression algorithm. Our test results presented are based on three algorithmic strategies and they surpass commercial software available on the market with a factor of almost 2:1.

articleTitle: Student cluster analysis based on Moodle data and academic performance indicators
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The present work considers the possibility of using Moodle course logs and student performance indicators within the Database Systems course to apply the K-Means clustering algorithm. Clusters of students are identified and explained to partition students with similar study behaviours and performance. Moreover, the understanding of the five groups emerged in cluster analysis allowed us to identify a cluster that contains 86% of students at risk of not completing the course activity. One important aspect that differentiates our study from other similar works is the use of data collected over a long period of time, from 2015 to 2019. The final data set, obtained after preprocessing, contains no less than 185.206 course logs.

articleTitle: Helios - an integrated platform for e-education
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A functional learning system is based on an efficient communication between the teacher and the learner. The current worldwide situation induced some drastic disruptions in the educational information transfer. Statistics taken from universities and schools revealed that many teachers and learners didn't adapt to the forced switch towards the digital environment. A new approach is needed in order to keep alive the learners' interest for the live or asynchronous educational material presentations, thus ensuring pedagogical continuity.

articleTitle: Experimental and Analytical Study of the Electric Potential using Lagrange Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Integrating abstract notions as electric potential are challenging engineering tasks to most students. The present paper proposes a practical experiment for describing the electrical field distribution using Lagrange's polynomials. First, we aim to exemplify that the interpolation polynomials are useful for the approximation of the electric potential, using the finite element method to outline the way the size of the finite element and the degree of the interpolation polynomials influence computational errors. Secondly, an experimental circuit board has been developed to enable students to measure effectively the electrostatic potential.

articleTitle: Simulation of Automotive MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article is based on the development of an automotive radar MIMO simulator to show the advantage of using a larger number of transmit and receive antennas. A simulation result obtained for a relative complex scenario, concerning multiple vehicles running on highway, proves the performance of the simulator.

articleTitle: Accurate Measurement of the rms of a Sine-wave by Means of Low-Cost rms-to-dc Convertes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper firstly a low-cost non-inverter half-wave rectifier (HWR)-based rms-to-dc converter is designed for the measurement of the root mean square (rms) of a sine-wave. The accuracy of this converter is investigated as a function of the resistance errors and the HWR op amp input offset voltage. Then, the accuracy of the designed HWR-based rms-to-dc converter is compared with that of a true rms-to-dc converter through experimental results as a function of the sine-wave magnitude and frequency. The true rms-to-dc converter is a new generation, low-cost, and low-power converter. The performed comparison allow us to determine the situations in which each of the above rms-to-dc converter is most suited to be used in practice.

articleTitle: Power Source of Sinusoidal Voltage and Variable Frequency
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A problem encountered in practice is related to the generation of sinusoidal electrical voltage with variable frequency. Generating a variable frequency voltage can be used in different applications as well as in the testing of asynchronous motors. As is known the speed of asynchronous motors depends on the frequency of the power supply to maintain a roughly constant torque. Power voltage value depends on the asynchronous motor type. The power source proposed in the paper is based on two large blocks, namely: a DC/DC convertor and an inverter stage. The DC/DC convertor can generate an output DC voltage of 310V or lower from an input DC voltage of 12 V. The output voltage of the DC/DC converter can be applied then to the inverter power stage obtaining in this case a sinusoidal voltage with amplitude close to 310 V and adjustable frequency. The circuit described in the paper was developed to be used in the learning process of the students that follow study programs in the field of electronics engineering.

articleTitle: Augmenting Learning through VR Storytelling
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a narrative instructional model as an interaction framework in a Virtual Reality environment. Virtual Reality solutions provide the means to present a storytelling scenario through visual interactive models. The proposed implementation consists of a VR prototype developed to assist kindergarten and primary school pupils, in assimilating knowledge about different types of musical instruments, while developing a sense of practice-based interaction. The application is structured on three levels; each level is represented by an element of nature (water, earth and air), corresponding to the know-how complexity: water or level 0 which reflects an elementary level of intrinsic knowledge; towards the "air environment" that reflects the level of cumulative knowledge that will be reached by the end of the game. Knowledge is assimilated by interacting with elements in the virtual environment and by following the annotated guidelines.

articleTitle: A New Buck Converter with Hybrid Switching
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Two new hybrid buck type converters are proposed. Compared to the classical buck converter, the proposed topologies provide a negative output voltage, while compared to the buck-boost converter semiconductor voltage stresses are lower. The coupled inductor version has the additional advantage of achieving a smaller conversion ratio for the same duty cycle value. The dc analysis is presented and design equations are developed. Simulation and experimental verifications confirm the feasibility of the new topologies.

articleTitle: Online versus On-site e-Assessment in Medical Education: are we ready for the change?
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We compared two E-assessment platforms and we evaluated the impact of online versus on-site examination by analysing students' outcomes and classifying them into performance groups. Two groups of 480 (G1/2019) and 527 (G2/2020) 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> year medical students were included. G1 was assessed by using E-School Exam Module on-site, while G2 used FlexiQuiz assessment platform online. G2 received 3 partial examinations during the semester while G1 was evaluated by o single final exam at the end of the semester. Students were classified in four performance categories as high (8-10, HPG), medium (6-7.99, MPG), low (5-5.99, LPG) and fail (less than 4, FPG) based on final grade. The analysis was applied for both theoretical and practical exams. A significant increase of HPG (79% vs 4% for theory and 42% vs 16% for practice) was noted for G2 compared with G1. MPG remained relatively the same between groups while LPG decreased for G2 compared with G1 (22% vs 1% for theory, 25% vs 4% for practice). The G2-FPG significantly decreased but remained higher for practical exam. HGP, LPG, FPG were strongly influenced by applying different assessment methods while MPG remained similar for G1 and G2. Factors influencing these variations will be discussed here.

articleTitle: Time-multiplexed 10Gbps Ethernet-based Integrated Logic Analyzer for FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We designed a time-multiplexed high-speed integrated logic analyzer (ILA) probing system for FPGA device technology, which is currently under implementation. The high-speed interface is a 10 Gbps Ethernet on fiber optics that connects the proposed ILA to the host computer. For the proposed design, we deduce the mathematical model for the performance. We report our preliminary test results, future work and conclusions.

articleTitle: Couchbase Server in Microsoft Azure Cloud: A Docker Container Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper evaluates the Couchbase Server platform performance for storing data items, using NoSQL databases. It involved services for querying and indexing, both deployed in Microsoft Azure Cloud environment and virtual machines. The architecture contained three virtual machines acting as nodes for the Couchbase Server database. Deploying and establishing the database in the public cloud was done with Docker images. Some of the key features and applications from Microsoft Azure were tested, i.e. Monitor, Resource groups, Dashboard and Storage accounts. From the Couchbase perspective, its friendly usage with full text search and real-time analytics proved to be useful for processing of big data.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Total Electron Content Prediction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The correction of ionospheric delay is an important part of insuring the precision of Global Navigation Satellite Systems. Real time measurements are taken by the various services at ground stations and broadcast to terminals for corrections. The correction works well for terrestrial areas near the stations but errors increase for marine measurements and remote terrestrial locations especially near the Equator. We attempt to create a neural network that can accurately infer the local Vertical Total Electron Content (VTEC) of a receiver from as few parameters as possible. To this end we use a neural network called IONONET that we attempt to improve by augmenting the training dataset with synthetic data from a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN).

articleTitle: Smart Mirror for Skin Type Identification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The use of unsuitable dermato-cosmetic products for a specific skin type may favor skin sensitization, or the development of a new dermatologic issue. This paper proposes a method to identify acne, blackheads, freckles, and normal skin types, limiting thus the evolution of these issues and increasing buyer satisfaction. It relies on a pre-trained MobileNet neural network, and runs on Raspberry Pi 4 model B with Coral USB Accelerator.

articleTitle: Disease detection on medical images using light-weight Convolutional Neural Networks for resource constrained platforms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough investigation to optimize light-weight convolutional neural networks for diseases detection from medical images. Particularly, we are interested in building an efficient recognition convolutional deep learning architecture running on portable, energy efficient, resources constrained platforms, as aids to medical personnel. Several state of the art light-weight deep neural network architectures as well as more complex (for better performance) ones were compared not only from the point of view of recognition accuracy but also from the complexity perspective. An original solution with Android and Raspberry-Pi implementations is proposed to give a good trade-off between complexity, detection accuracy, latency and portability in building intelligent medical instruments. Experiments on the Chest X-ray dataset indicate that our proposed solutions achieves state of the art accuracies with 91.22% less trainable parameters and with 3.62 times less memory usage storage, when compared with other state of the art light weight models.

articleTitle: Color fractal texture image complexity estimation using a convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we analyze the capacity of a convolutional neural network (CNN) to understand and model color texture. More specifically, we ask the question if a CNN is able to predict the complexity of a color texture image, in particular of a color fractal image. We used color entropy and color fractal dimension to compute the complexity of both natural color texture images from the VisTex image data base and synthetic color fractal images. We modified the last layer of a ResNet-18 CNN so that the network outputs a real number representing the input image complexity expressed either as color entropy or color fractal dimension. We trained the modified ResNet CNN in two scenarios: when fractal images were not part of the training set and when they were part of the training set. We report on our experimental results and draw the conclusions.

articleTitle: Advanced Quantization Methods for CNNs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this article, methods are presented that improve a quantization procedure for the inference of convolutional neural networks with respect to the resulting accuracy and resource requirements. The existing procedure is extended by pre-training, fine tuning and a suitable compression method. With the presented methods we get better convergence properties for deep quantized networks, we increase the accuracy by a several percentage points and we reduce the number of parameters by up to 90% depending on the model used.

articleTitle: Efficient analysis of digital systems' supplied data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Nowadays, when digital systems supply a lot of information, it is impossible for human operators to analyze it and to extract conclusions without using automation mechanisms. Thus, advances in data processing became the aim of many entities both in Industry and Academia. In order to supply reliable reports to customers and target public, each institution must take into account two important aspects: which are peculiarities of managed data and which algorithms can be used to extract most of information from it. The proficiency to extract correct trends from collected data makes entities to gain market share in lot of domains (e.g. statistics, forecasting activities). For this reason, a lot of efforts are directed in scientific research for analysis of data coming from digital devices, using also a concept which achieved good results in many branches of industry: machine learning.

articleTitle: Smart Illumination for Large Area Buildings Using RF Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In the present work we propose the development of an intelligent lighting system aimed to be used in large area buildings and taking as example some buildings of the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca (Romania). The system incorporates several modules, each module replacing a lighting switch in the building. The purpose of these modules is to control the lighting fixtures in the hallways of the buildings according to the movement in the covered area and the light intensity. The modules communicate with each other by radio communication, through a tree structure. All modules transmit information to the central node consisting of an Arduino Uno development board and the NRF24L01 radio communication module. The central node transmits the serial information via USB connection to the PC, where the information is processed by a custom program developed to display information related to the status of the modules and to control the modules remotely.

articleTitle: About the possibility to use the model based testing for system test automation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents the basic concept of using model-based testing to define and generate automated testes for automotive systems. It is described the development of model-based testing for the fuel level indication and the application of the model in the system testing. For developing the model, we define a consume curve of the fuel level and the results of the model are used in developing automated testing using an internal tool (uTAS) for the testing at the system level.

articleTitle: A New Step-Up Watkins-Johnson Type Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: A new step-up Watkins-Johnson (W-J) type converter is derived and analyzed in this paper. Starting from the origin of the converter, the new topology is derived using cell rotation, then the calculation of the static conversion ratio along with dc inductor currents and capacitor voltages, the small signal analysis and the deduction of the control-to-output and audiosusceptibility transfer functions are performed. Knowing that the new converter operates with a duty cycle less than 0.5, all mathematical equations are derived along with computer simulations. The simulation results fully verify the theoretical considerations and validate the feasibility of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Communication and Verification for Radar Sensors in the Context of Driver Assistance Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Automotive industry is a very large industry across the globe and nowadays all about designing and manufacturing innovative solutions are for a safe, comfortable, and efficient driving experience. It is important to include radar sensors in driver assistance systems because can increase the safety for the driver, passengers, and pedestrians. The paper is focused on communication between radar sensors, presents a new approach for transmitting large data between the nodes. In order to test if the radar sensors are well packed and prepared for commercial use, a software solution is offered.

articleTitle: Local binary patterns and Fourier transform based hyperspectral image classification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel classification framework based on a parallel architecture with Local Binary Pattern techniques and Fourier transform models. The Local Binary Pattern model is used as a descriptor employed on the spatial domain of the hyperspectral data. The Fourier transform method is applied along the spectral dimension of the hyperspectral set for each pixel in order to evaluate the data in terms of magnitude spectrum. Our proposed model is based on the concatenation of these types of spectral and spatial descriptors, for a more accurate classification of the data. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can improve the accuracy on Indian Pines and Pavia University sets even with a limited number of training samples with a reduced computation time.

articleTitle: Automotive Lead-Acid Battery Supplied DC-DC Power Converter with Variable Output Voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This article presents how one can supply equipment which requires a regulated output and low ripple voltage such as HAM radios, which require a regulated 13.7V, by using a switch mode DC\DC converter powered up from an automotive battery. Car batteries can output 11.31V to 12.7V in normal state and cannot be fed to HAM radio equipment since they require 13.7V. Specially designed switch mode DC/DC converters with super low current and voltage ripple are required to supply them.

articleTitle: A Novel VLSI Algorithm for a Low Complexity VLSI Implementation of DCT Based on Pseudo Circular Correlation Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel VLSI algorithm for a low complexity VLSI implementation of DCT based on pseudo circular correlation structures. The proposed method introduces an algorithm which has a computational structure with a low complexity, leading naturally to a low complexity of the hardware.

articleTitle: Spectral Component Analysis of Magnetically Unshielded Magnetocardiograms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The novel coronavirus pandemic has risen the challenge to find new health analysis techniques and devices. Magneto-cardiograms acquire information about the electric activity of the heart, displaying a richer frequency spectrum than the classical electrocardiograms. We will analyze the biological data from a new viewpoint, checking the frequency band of the signal using wavelets and Welch's method. The Power Spectral Density is used as an objective estimate of the power components distribution over the frequency range. We aim to develop adaptive and efficient filtering procedures. The results display a neater signal, more useful for diagnosis.

articleTitle: To “paint“ with Human Tissues and Modern Technology: This is Art in Histology Gamification
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Keeping students motivated in conditions of social distancing is a real challenge for teachers. The use of alternative methods that are not perceived as a conventional way of learning increases student's curiosity. The game is a method of relaxation at any age, nowadays often combined with modern technology. Gamification is an alternative learning method increasingly applied in higher medical education for developing medical students' practical skills. The online distance learning has challenged us to apply gamification in histology. We launched a competition for 2nd year medical students having as first award Romanian edition of the worldwide known histology book. In May 2020, in the middle of COVID 19 pandemic, we asked students to review our Case-Center histological slides from their own perspective, to select those tissues which resemble to anything from real life and to do art using modern technology. A Facebook page was created for posting students works. Students created high quality works using tissue pieces, their unlimited imagination and modern technology. We received 181 pictures, one animation and 3 videos with a brief message attached. A stunning compilation of Art in Histology competition works created a book entitled "181 HISTOries from 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> year medical students during COVID19 pandemic".

articleTitle: Soft Switched Multiphase Converter with Parallel Resonant DC-Link Circuit
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The paper presents a soft switched multiphase DC/DC converter with a parallel resonant dc-link (PRDCL) circuit. First, the circuit function is described using a single- phase converter, the circuit analysis is then extended to interleaved multiphase converter. The challenge is to control the soft switching operation of several phases utilizing one resonant dc- link circuit The mathematical analysis is completed by numerous simulations. Finally,the feasibility of that circuit is proved by a 2 kW, two phase buck converter with PRDCL prototype.

articleTitle: Keeping the subthreshold all along the transients. The WTA unbounded domain case
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper considers the basic Lazzaro Winner Take All circuit. In order to force all voltage trajectories in weak inversion domain, the invariance conditions for the ODE model are employed. Tractable relations between circuit parameters and input currents are inferred and numerically checked.

articleTitle: A Novel Single Switch Step-Up Converter with High Conversion Ratio
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper, a new boost converter topology consisting of one active switch and two diodes is presented. The proposed topology preserves the smooth current at the input and additionally provides a smooth output current. Compared to the classical boost it provides a higher step-up conversion ratio at the same duty cycle. The dc analysis is performed in order to obtain the main equations in steady state. After the evaluation of the device stresses, the features of the proposed converter are presented in comparison to other step-up topologies. Using the design equations, the converter was properly designed and then simulated. The simulation results confirmed the theoretical considerations and the feasibility of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: ARM Embedded Low Cost Solution for Implementing Deep Learning Paradigms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have become a topic of great interest to scientific research groups due to their applicability in a wide range of fields. Advanced technologies of both software and integrated hardware have led to the possibility of implementing and running deep neural network models directly at the data source, on general purpose microcontrollers, resulting in a significant cost reduction at the system level. The purpose of this work is to implement and benchmark a deep neural network architecture on a bare metal system using a low-cost and energy-efficient STM32F779I-EVAL board with an ARM Cortex-M7 core and CMSIS-NN software kernels.

articleTitle: An Application of Automation Solutions in Dynamically Water Supply Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Reconfigurable technological process automation solutions may represent the key for overcoming difficulties encountered by developing economies. In order to speed up the above mentioned process design and preliminary tests could be accelerated using IT simulation with the help of virtual instrumentation. For exemplifying this approach we discuss in this paper an application, based on virtual instrumentation formalisms for modeling a network for water supply.

articleTitle: An Overview of Sign-On Risks and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper is intended to present the vulnerabilities of the sign-on methods especially those caused by users when trying to access various network services using a single account and the same password for all of them. The sign-on process is more secure by the mean of two-factor authentication and different security standards but still there are some weaknesses that need to be eliminated so different solutions, new or already used, are discussed in order to increase the security level of the access to the network.

articleTitle: Auto-Generative Learning Objects for Learning Linked Lists Concepts
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: Generative Learning Objects are reusable educational templates to be filled with learning content. Currently, they are used only in experimental environments and not on a large scale like multiple-choice questions. One reason for this drawback is the complexity of meta-models that teachers should imagine and write. In this sense, several example instances are provided and we selected the linked list concept taught in the context of Data Structures and Algorithms discipline. We outline several use cases of the linked lists and their corresponding models.

articleTitle: A survey on outlier detection methods applied on air quality data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the impact of various time series prediction algorithms applied on air quality data. This data is obtained from several sensors measurements, at every passing minute. The current research is concerned about finding a solution for a prediction algorithm based on fit functions. Traditional statistics models such as ARIMA (AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average Model) and modern ones, like Facebook Prophet, were used for a comparative approach. Moreover, our proposed method has also been tested using different types of regression: Linear, Polynomial and Spline. After having made all the possible analogies between the selected algorithms for the given time series, regression spline has been found as the most accurate model. The purpose of this paper is to explain and to convince that results behave in a different manner depending on the used algorithm. The research has been done by studying air quality measurements received from various sensors, such as: PM2.5, PM1, PM10, O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O, temperature, pressure and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The study analyses sensors' values over a period of several months, obtaining over 43000 measurements per month for each sensor. The paper discusses the data obtained and its accuracy is tested using various metrics of evaluation.

articleTitle: About the positivity of trigonometric polynomials with positive samples
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we focus on the class of trigonometric polynomials that have positive samples at frequency points that are multiples of 2π/N. It has previously been shown that this cannot guarantee the positivity of a polynomial trigonometric. We discuss some aspects that can affect the positivity: the influence of sample scattering, the weight of the number of samples and the effect of minor changes to the samples. Usually, scattering the samples increases the chance that the polynomial trigonometry will not be positive. The number of samples is not very important, and its weight almost disappears when the variance of the samples is small. If the values of the samples change very little, the positivity of the polynomial trigonometric is not affected.

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Compressive Sensing Algorithms for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: We analyze the possibility of using compressive sensing algorithms for the rapid chirps waveform in automotive radar sensor applications. Two algorithms are considered: Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and l1-magic. We compare the two methods in a scenario using nine targets, with and without noise. The number of non-uniformly placed samples is four times less than the number of uniform samples, with target detection possible even in the presence of noise. It is shown that OMP outperforms l1-magic, with spectra not affected by the Compressive Sensing reconstruction. The results are comparable with the traditional uniform sampling results.

articleTitle: Single Tier Heterogeneous Traffic Generator based on Traffic Statistics
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The most dedicated mathematical tool for spatial traffic modeling is based on stochastic geometry and consider base stations (BSs) and the user equipment (UE) locations modeled as two independent Poisson point processes (PPP). This approach is a relatively good model for generating BS locations but has a major drawback in modelling UE locations due to the lack of adjustability in representing the severity of nonuniformity of the UE position. The second issue is represented by the lack of correlation between the two independent PPPs. The present work reviews different adjustable traffic statistics used in heterogenous traffic generation, along with a novel proposed statistic: the spatial autocorrelation of the users. Only two parameters are used for traffic generation (Coefficient of Variation and the Correlation Coefficient between UE and BS). The proposed traffic generation model capabilities are illustrated in a single tier wireless cellular network.

articleTitle: LTE Band Filtering Applications of a Fractal Based Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: In this paper we explore possibilities to tailor the transmittance of frequency selective surfaces (FSS's) realized on printed circuit boards (PCB's) to match design requirements by duplication of the metal pattern and fractalization. An FSS based on a novel unit cell structure is introduced, which is shown to exhibit angular stability up to 60° for TE and 45° for TM case. For the evaluation of the fine-tuning capabilities, a parametric study is performed. The configuration can be used for filtering in LTE, Wi-Fi and X band, commonly used in Automotive environment.

articleTitle: The Design of a Crowd Density Checker App in Android with People Localization Using the GPS from the Mobile Device
publicationTitle: 2020 International Symposium on Electronics and Telecommunications (ISETC)
abstract: The aim of this work focuses on checking the density of people in a certain place. The idea behind is based on the fact that almost every person has a mobile device with GPS, so getting the coordinated from the mobile device, can get the coordinates of the person owning it. The coordinates can be placed on a map and united them in clusters, to know the number of persons in a specific place. The app can useful to avoid big crowds of not. Sometimes it is needed to avoid big crowds of people when going shopping or in traffic. Other times it is not needed to avoid big crowds, because where many people are, something is happening, big sales, good concerts or good mood in a bar.
